shared_elements: low-relief carving on an upright rectangular slab/stele
animal forms (quadruped, bird) in A; bird-headed staff element in B
repeated small motifs arranged in rows
justification: Both are upright slabs bearing low-relief profile imagery divided into horizontal registers, and both include a bird-like form, but that is about as generic as such correspondence gets. A shows a purely zoomorphic repertoire — rows of crouching animals, a quadruped, a snake-like/net band, a large long-necked bird — with no human presence, whereas B is dominated by a single richly costumed standing human figure holding a staff/parasol, flanked by columns of repeated sign-blocks that read as script; the subject matter and organising logic are essentially different.
